title: Nüfus Address Registration (Adres Kayıt Sistemi) After Getting Ikamet
seoTitle: Nüfus Address Registration After Ikamet in Türkiye (2026)
metaDescription: Register your Turkish residence address within 20 working days after Ikamet. Exact documents, 2026 fines, and moving rules for expats.
quickAnswer: Foreign residents in Türkiye must register their residential address in the Adres Kayıt Sistemi (AKS) within 20 working days of receiving an Ikamet card or entering on a consular permit. Missing this deadline triggers a 2026 administrative fine of 814 TL and can block future permit renewals, bank updates, and local utility contracts.

body.text: Receiving your Turkish residence permit card feels like the finish line, yet one critical administrative step remains: recording where you actually live in the national [Adres Kayıt Sistemi (AKS)](https://www.nvi.gov.tr/adres-kayit-sistemi). Without an active address record, your Ikamet sits incomplete in government databases, creating friction when you renew your permit, enroll children in school, or verify residency with banks.

How many days (20 working days) do you have to register your address at Nüfus Müdürlüğü?

Under Law No. 5490 and [Presidency of Migration Management guidelines](https://en.goc.gov.tr/frequently-asked-questions-about-foreigners), you have exactly 20 working days to register your address. The clock starts on the date your residence permit is notified or delivered inside Türkiye, or from your date of entry if you obtained a consular residence or work permit abroad.

Working days exclude weekends and Turkish public holidays. Because appointment slots at provincial migration offices and district population directorates fill quickly in Istanbul, Ankara, and Antalya, book your appointment through the [Göç Randevu Sistemi](https://www.goc.gov.tr/yenilenen-goc-randevu-sistemi) or check your local district Nüfus Müdürlüğü workflow as soon as your card arrives. First-time foreign address registrations in major provinces are routinely processed at Provincial Directorate of Migration Management (İl Göç İdaresi) address desks before syncing with NVİ.

body.text: What exact documents (notarized lease, utility bill or landlord consent, passport, Ikamet) are required?

Officers verify both your legal identity and your physical right to occupy the apartment. Bring your valid passport, original Ikamet card (with your 99-series foreigner ID number), and proof of residence: either a notarized rental contract, a title deed (Tapu) with a current numbering certificate (Numarataj), or a notarized landlord/host undertaking (Taahhütname).

Officers also require a recent utility bill (electricity, water, or natural gas) issued in your name for that exact address, or proof that the apartment is vacant in AKS. If another person is still registered at your flat, the system blocks your entry until that prior resident is removed or the landlord appears with you.

items: Original passport plus photocopy of the bio page and latest entry stamp
Original Ikamet card (or active work permit card) showing your 99-series ID number
Notarized lease agreement signed by both landlord and tenant (or Tapu if you own the property)
Recent electricity, water, or gas bill in your name (or a notarized host undertaking plus host ID if living with a partner or friend)
Printed appointment confirmation from [Göç Randevu Sistemi](https://www.goc.gov.tr/yenilenen-goc-randevu-sistemi) or district Nüfus Müdürlüğü
Official UAVT 10-digit address code (confirmable via [NVİ Adres Hizmetleri](https://www.nvi.gov.tr/adres-hizmetleri))

body.text: What happens if your address is not registered on time?

Missing the 20-working-day deadline incurs a 2026 administrative fine of 814 TL under Article 68 of Law No. 5490, while declaring a false address triggers a 17,051 TL penalty according to [2026 Turkish consular updates](https://salzburg-bk.mfa.gov.tr/Mission/ShowInfoNote/412331). Beyond fines, an unregistered address can stall Ikamet renewals and trigger police verification visits.

Because e-Residence renewal portals cross-check AKS records automatically, an unrecorded address frequently causes extension applications to be rejected or delayed. If you plan to apply for long-term residency or citizenship later, gaps in your registered address history create avoidable legal complications.
How do you update your address when moving apartments?

Whenever you move to a new apartment within the same province, you must report your new address within 20 working days using your new notarized lease and utility bill. If you relocate to a different province altogether, [Presidency of Migration Management rules](https://en.goc.gov.tr/frequently-asked-questions-about-foreigners) require filing a residence permit transfer application in the new province within 20 working days.

Once your address is updated, download your new Yerleşim Yeri (Residence Certificate) through e-Devlet to confirm the 10-digit UAVT code matches your lease. Also check whether the neighborhood you are moving to is open to new foreign registrations before signing a rental contract.

faq.q: Can I register my address before my physical Ikamet card arrives?
faq.a: No. You need your approved foreigner ID number (starting with 99) and physical residence or work permit card before provincial migration or Nüfus officers can enter your address into the Adres Kayıt Sistemi.

faq.q: What if a previous tenant is still registered at my new apartment?
faq.a: The AKS system blocks duplicate registrations by unrelated parties. Bring your notarized lease and a utility bill in your name to the district Nüfus Müdürlüğü so officers can initiate an address verification and remove the former occupant.

faq.q: Can foreigners update their address online via e-Devlet?
faq.a: In some cases, holders of an active e-Devlet password with SMS verification or an e-signature can view or initiate updates, as noted on [NVİ Address FAQ](https://www.nvi.gov.tr/sss-adres-hizmetleri). However, foreign residents moving leases usually need an in-person document check at İl Göç İdaresi or Nüfus Müdürlüğü.

faq.q: Does owning property in Türkiye automatically register my address?
faq.a: No. Buying a home gives you a Tapu (title deed), not an AKS entry. You must still register your residential address within 20 working days of receiving your Ikamet using your Tapu and a current Numarataj (numbering document) from the municipality.

faq.q: Do I pay the Ikamet fee again if I move to another Turkish province?
faq.a: According to Presidency of Migration Management rules, if your residence permit type stays the same when you transfer to a new province within 20 working days, you receive an updated card without repaying the underlying permit fee for the remaining duration.

faq.q: Can I register at a friend's apartment if I am staying there temporarily?
faq.a: Only if you genuinely live there and the host provides a notarized undertaking (Taahhütname) or appears with you at the office with their ID and utility bill. Declaring an address where you do not reside carries a 17,051 TL fine in 2026 and jeopardizes your permit.
